facts.fact: Gauri gave Kunal two red-thread walnuts, one for Mini's string and one for Ila; Kunal ties Ila's to her short brass surveyor's chain at her belt with his teeth.
facts.why: needed because the beat has Kunal tie a red-thread walnut to her surveyor's chain.

facts.fact: Kiran crossed the Saddle with the hill council pairs (Roop's crew) at the thaw, at Ila's summons, and stands in the cairn ring when the rubbing is read.
facts.why: needed because Kiran must be present at the cairn reading and Ila promised him first word.

facts.fact: Bindu reads the worn final glyph on the rubbing as the crew knot-song sign for the day a pattern is loosed, the thaw, so the line reads 'carried till no thaw'.
facts.why: needed because the beat has Bindu read the old script via knot-songs.

facts.fact: Pritam escaped Garh Neshar's tower by a hidden stair behind the north-wall plaster between the landing and lower room, to the kitchen passage and a postern whose key someone gave him; he left with about six men and a pony string, heading east up the dry side.
facts.why: needed because the beat has Pritam escape via the void Ila measured.

facts.fact: The queen seals the Under-Cairn under day-and-night warden guard at the gap and the crawl's mouth until the fourth winter has passed.
facts.why: needed because the beat orders the Under-Cairn guarded.

facts.fact: Lata arrives at the Kothi Shilak salt house at thaw with a Taravan convoy, after two days in Ranu where she heard the story of the grey-bearded officer; Nimmi refused to name him ('not mine to spend').
facts.why: needed because the beat teases Lata's early convoy and her question to Meera.
